context.text: Hey Leo! 15 minutes of Project Hail Mary in bed at 9:30, phone on the dresser. A quick voice note when you're done.

transcript.text: [voice: Done, page 81 of Project Hail Mary.]
Leo! Page 81 and day 3 in a row 📚 That's 23 pages tonight, your biggest night yet. What's pulling you into Project Hail Mary right now?
read way past 15 min tonight, got to the part where he figures out the beetles thing. couldn't stop
Ha, the beetles part is a good one. Phone on the dresser and you still went way past 15, so what made it easy to keep going tonight?
it's the problem solving. every chapter he's stuck and then he works it out and I want to know how

That's a great thing to notice about yourself, Leo. A book where every chapter has a problem and a payoff keeps you turning pages. When Project Hail Mary ends, what would you want next that gives you that same pull?
yeah honestly the phone on the dresser is the whole trick, if it's next to me I'm on it in 2 minutes

Two minutes is a real tell, Leo, and you've set up your night around it 🔥 Tomorrow, Tuesday, same 9:30 in bed with the phone on the dresser. Read 15 minutes, then send a voice note with your page number and one problem he's stuck on. Work for you?
I think it's also that I picked a book I actually wanted to read, not one I thought I should

Picking a book you actually want is half the battle, Leo, and the phone on the dresser protects the other half. That's two rules you worked out yourself 💪 Tomorrow, Tuesday: 15 minutes at 9:30 in bed, phone on the dresser, then a voice note with your page number and one problem he's stuck on. Work for you?
true. and I sleep better when I read instead of scrolling

Reading beats scrolling for your sleep too, Leo, and you're noticing it yourself. Three nights, three rules you worked out on your own 🔥 Tomorrow, Tuesday: 15 minutes at 9:30 in bed, phone on the dresser, then a voice note with your page number and one problem he's stuck on. Are you in?
sounds good
Locked in, Leo. Tomorrow at 9:30: phone on the dresser, 15 minutes, then the voice note. Enjoy the rest of the beetles 🪲
